about: The memories from my final two years after Ballroom Year, dominated by Candy Year, when an injury changed how I experienced State Arts-In and the pain, people, work, and ridiculous moments forged some of my strongest memories.
body: CDIFBIF FCCFBICFCAIJBEH DIBBEHFE brings together memories from my final two years in State Arts-In after Ballroom Year. Most of them come from Candy Year, when I went into the fair injured and experienced SAI very differently than I had before.

A broken ankle and a knee scooter became part of everyday life that year. I couldn't move around the fair the way I normally would, ordinary things became harder, and sometimes it simply hurt. But in a strange way, that pain helped forge the memories. The things that happened around me, the people who stayed with me, and the moments that broke through the discomfort became some of the stories that stuck with me the strongest.

That included Lauren covering me and my knee scooter in hazard tape, working on the candy oven, and Paul trusting me to understand my own limits instead of treating the injury as a reason I couldn't contribute. Then repeated nighttime fire alarms turned getting out of the building on an injured ankle into yet another part of the experience. Friends stayed behind on the stairs, helped when I needed it, and turned situations that could have simply been miserable into memories worth keeping.

Mixed among those are the friendships, inside jokes, and traditions that had accumulated after years of State Arts-In, including a family tree that made absolutely no sense but somehow made perfect sense to us.

There is comparatively little from my final year. I knew my time in State Arts-In was coming to an end, and looking back, I think I may have subconsciously started separating myself before I actually had to leave. One of the memories that did remain was Kenny giving me a dartboard as a graduation gift, something that still hangs on my wall.

These songs capture the last stretch of my State Arts-In story, but especially Candy Year. It was a year shaped by an injury I never wanted, yet the pain, friendships, trust, and absurd moments surrounding it forged memories that have lasted far longer than the injury itself.
